speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific signs of respiratory distress you are observing in this newborn, such as cyanosis, grunting, or retractions? Have there been any known maternal infections or complications during the pregnancy or delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the prematurity and rapid onset of distress, have you noticed specific signs like nasal flaring, grunting, or visible retractions around the ribs or supraclavicular area? Also, has the baby passed meconium or is there a history of polyhydramnios?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

The clinical picture of a 33-week preterm infant presenting with respiratory distress, grunting, and significant retractions 2 hours after birth is classic for RDS due to surfactant deficiency. The mention of tuberculosis is incorrect given the acute onset and gestational age; TB does not present this rapidly in a newborn without prolonged exposure history or congenital syphilis-like symptoms. We do not need to pursue TB testing further, but I will confirm the lung pathology with an imaging study. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
